close_reason: Public plain-map construction now returns canonical bottom on a final uninhabited required field without an extra scan, while preserving duplicate-key replacement semantics.
description:
Goal: Return canonical bottom from public plain-map construction when its final required field map contains canonical bottom, without adding a second traversal or changing duplicate-key resolution.

Signal: `Types::map` always gives its input iterator to `Descr::map_of`, which builds an ordered `BTreeMap`, then enters generic descriptor normalization. A plain map requires every listed field; a final field whose `Ty` is `none` makes the product uninhabited. This is the map analogue of the tuple product law, but input pairs can repeat a key, so an earlier bottom may be overwritten by a later inhabited value.

Strategy: Build the final ordered field map once, as today. Account for final bottom-valued fields as each insertion replaces or adds a value, so the completed map tells us whether it is impossible without a second value scan. Transfer the exact `BTreeMap` into `Descr::map_of`; return `none` before descriptor normalization if the final count is nonzero. Do not add a cache, hash, deep comparison, or a broad map-DNF cleanup.

TDD: First prove an interior final bottom field currently goes through interning work. Preserve the duplicate-key case where a later inhabited value overwrites an earlier bottom. Green proof must show no interning work for the final-bottom case.

Docs and acceptance: Explain the required-field product law and duplicate resolution constraint. Run focused type tests and enum/f98 canaries, fmt, check, strict Clippy, full workspace tests, cold branch-base review, one commit, draft stacked PR, and close.
title: Return impossible maps before descriptor normalization
